key_insight: A three-dimensional model predicts substantial angular variation in energy dissipation within equal-jet collisions, even with uniform inlet and sheet mean velocities.
engineering_relevance: Resolving angular differences in dissipation could help engineers assess mixing conditions in impinging-jet devices beyond a single overall dissipation rate.
method: Model collision-region thickness as varying linearly along radial lines from the stagnation point to the boundary.
Combine modeled volume with collision-induced kinetic energy loss to calculate dissipation per unit mass.
Calculate overall and narrow-angular-sector-averaged dissipation rates.
evidence_signal: The model recovers expected theoretical limits, including a cylindrical collision region for directly opposed jets, and preliminary micromixing results are consistent with its predicted angular variation.
watch_item: The assumed collision-region geometry and the actual location of energy dissipation still require independent validation.
paper_title: Azimuthally Resolved Energy Dissipation Rates in the Impingement Zone of Equal Free Impinging Liquid Jets: A Three-Dimensional Model
